subject: Re: Proposal — availability baseline, latency tiers, and batched-inference carveout
messages:
From: Jack Morton <jack.morton@novacorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — uptime baseline and credits for high-burst inference

Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Novacorp is excited about Redwood but we need to align on firm commitments for availability and latency before we can move to procurement. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Baseline uptime: we currently have a requirement for 99.95% across US regions. We may accept 99.9% if there are meaningful monthly remedies.
2) Batched/queued inference carveout: our workload is bursty with 30–40% of traffic benefiting from batching. We want to ensure that queued/batching behavior (which can look like transient higher latency) doesn't trigger full monthly credits unless there is sustained unavailability.

Can Redwood propose a template that includes a standard uptime, a latency tier (p95/p99), and an explicit carveout for batching? Also please include a simple monthly credit schedule so procurement can evaluate.

Appreciate a short proposal — attaching a one-page summary of our SRE concerns.

Best,
Jack
SRE Lead — Novacorp
[attachment: novacorp-sre-notes.txt (text)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Morton <jack.morton@novacorp.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — uptime baseline and credits for high-burst inference

Jack — thanks for the clear asks and the SRE notes. High level response below; Ben and Laura will add pricing/legal detail.

Summary of our suggested approach:
- Uptime baseline: Redwood proposes a 99.95% regional availability baseline for standard hosted tiers. For customers choosing reserved/dedicated capacity we can consider 99.99% (separate contract).
- Monthly credits: sliding remedy tied to percent below baseline (see short table below). Cap at 50% of monthly hosting fees.
- Batching carveout: transient latency spikes caused by automatic batching/queueing won’t count toward availability breaches provided they meet the "workload-aware batching" threshold (defined below). Sustained service degradation (errors, connection failures, or inability to serve requests for >30 continuous minutes) will count.
- Latency tiers: we offer target p95 and p99 windows by default (p95 < 250ms, p99 < 800ms for single-region API calls). Credits may apply if both error and latency SLOs are violated for a sustained window.

Draft monthly credit schedule (hosted):
- 99.95% and above: 0% credit
- 99.9% — 99.95%: 5% of monthly invoice
- 99.5% — 99.9%: 20% of monthly invoice
- <99.5%: 50% of monthly invoice (cap)

Batching carveout (proposal):
- Define batched-inference window: when >25% of requests are queued > 200ms waiting for batching, we will exclude those queued-only time windows from hourly availability calculation, provided the following hold:
  * No request failures (5xx) attributable to the service
  * Overall request completion for the hour remains within 110% of baseline throughput
  * Customer has enabled the Redwood batching profile; requests flagged as low-priority by the customer are excluded from credit calculations

Next steps: Ben will provide a clean PDF with the formal table and credit math; Laura will add suggested contract language for the carveout. Can you confirm Novacorp is comfortable with a 50% monthly cap?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

— Stephanie
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Morton <jack.morton@novacorp.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — uptime baseline and credits for high-burst inference

Jack — adding the numbers and an example monthly credit calc so procurement has a concrete datapoint. See short worked example below.

Assumptions (monthly hosting fee = $120k):
- If availability = 99.92% (i.e., 0.03% below 99.95%) => falls in 99.9–99.95 band => 5% credit => $6,000 credit
- If availability = 99.82% => 20% credit => $24,000 credit

Why a cap: the cap at 50% prevents negative incentives; it’s consistent with peer practice. We are open to escrowed credits or a remediation service credit bucket for larger enterprise deals.

Regarding batching carveout operationally:
- We propose Redwood provide a daily CSV (or API feed) that shows queued-duration histograms and the percent of requests affected. That dataset will be used jointly to evaluate whether a given hour meets the carveout exclusion.
- If Novacorp wants stricter rules (e.g., lower queued threshold or no carveout), we can flip to a dedicated pool pricing with SLA 99.99% instead.

Attached: short spreadsheet showing credit math and a sample call log extract.

— Ben Carter
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: novacorp-sla-comment-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Morton <jack.morton@novacorp.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — uptime baseline and credits for high-burst inference

Jack / Priya — quick legal note on carveouts and definitions to avoid downstream ambiguity. Suggested redline bullets to be added to the SLA: 

1) Definitions section: explicitly define "queued/awaiting batching" as the time between request ingress and start-of-inference compute, measured server-side in our telemetry.
2) Exclusion window: carveout applies only when queued-time median for the hour >200ms AND queued requests represent >=25% of total ingress; otherwise the hour is eligible for availability calculation.
3) Measurement and audit: Redwood will provide the raw telemetry and a one-week lookback within 48 hours upon request; if disputed, both parties will engage an independent third-party auditor (mutually agreed) — costs split 50/50.
4) Emergency maintenance: Redwood will provide notice windows for planned maintenance; unplanned emergency maintenance will be communicated within 2 hours and will not be treated as an availability breach if the event is restricted to maintenance actions and we route or failover per our runbook.

If Novacorp is ok with these points, we will bake precise definitions into the SLA document. If Novacorp requires a lower cap than 50% or custom carveout thresholds, please flag it and we’ll route to the deal desk for special approval.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Jack Morton <jack.morton@novacorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — uptime baseline and credits for high-burst inference

Team — thanks, this is very helpful and clearer than I expected. Two quick points from procurement/SRE: 

1) Cap: procurement would prefer a 40% cap rather than 50% for hosted services. Is that a firm no or something you can escalate?
2) Measurement: the proposed telemetry feed + one-week lookback looks good — procurement will want the CSV schema and a test dataset so our SREs can validate parsing before signature.

We’re available for a 30-min call Wednesday 10–11am PT to finalize thresholds; please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Jack
SRE Lead — Novacorp
